boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named UNH spaces for studying, meeting, making media, playing games, or taking a quiet break between classes.

cards.title: Hubbard Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Dimond Library, Level 3
cards.notes: Use this designated quiet area for individual reading or focused work; keep calls and audible devices outside the space.
cards.short_summary: A named quiet-study room on Dimond Library’s main floor.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH Libraries lists the Hubbard Reading Room on Dimond Library Level 3 as a designated quiet space for individual study.
cards.source_title: Spaces to Study & Work | UNH Library
cards.access_notes: Follow current Dimond Library access rules and quiet-area expectations.

cards.title: Addison Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Dimond Library, Level 3
cards.notes: Bring a solo task and use the designated quiet setting; move conversations or phone calls to an approved area.
cards.short_summary: A second named quiet-study room on Dimond’s main floor.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH Libraries identifies the Addison Reading Room on Dimond Library Level 3 as a designated quiet area for individual study.
cards.source_title: Spaces to Study & Work | UNH Library
cards.access_notes: Follow current Dimond Library access rules and quiet-area expectations.

cards.title: Courtyard Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Dimond Library, Level 5
cards.notes: Head to Level 5 when you need a designated quiet-study setting and can work independently without conversation.
cards.short_summary: A named Level 5 quiet space inside Dimond Library.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH Libraries lists the Courtyard Reading Room on Dimond Library Level 5 among its designated quiet spaces.
cards.source_title: Spaces to Study & Work | UNH Library
cards.access_notes: Follow current Dimond Library access rules and quiet-area expectations.

cards.title: Parker Media Lab
cards.subtitle: Dimond Library, Room 257
cards.notes: Plan a media-focused work session here; confirm current equipment availability or assistance needs with library staff first.
cards.short_summary: A named media-work destination on Dimond Library’s second level.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH Libraries lists Parker Media Lab, Room 257, on Level 2 of Dimond Library.
cards.source_title: Dimond Library | UNH Library
cards.access_notes: Check current library access and any equipment-use requirements before visiting.

cards.title: Studio 235
cards.subtitle: Dimond Library, Level 2
cards.notes: Use the library floor listing to locate this named studio, then check locally for current setup and availability.
cards.short_summary: A named studio destination on Dimond Library’s second level.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH Libraries lists Studio 235 on Level 2 of Dimond Library.
cards.source_title: Dimond Library | UNH Library
cards.access_notes: Check current library access and room-use requirements before visiting.

cards.title: Games Room
cards.subtitle: Memorial Union Building, Room 154A
cards.notes: Meet a friend for billiards, table tennis, or video games in Room 154A; verify the room’s current availability on arrival.
cards.short_summary: A named MUB room for casual table and video games.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH’s MUB venues page says the Games Room in Room 154A offers billiards, table tennis, and video games.
cards.source_title: Venues & Services | Memorial Union & Student Activities
cards.access_notes: Room availability may vary with MUB operations and scheduled use.

cards.title: Commuter Lounge
cards.subtitle: Memorial Union Building, first floor
cards.notes: Commuting students can use the couches, tables, whiteboard, and charging station during regular MUB hours.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor MUB multipurpose lounge for commuting students.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH states that its first-floor MUB Commuter Lounge provides commuters with couches, tables, chairs, a whiteboard, and a charging station.
cards.source_title: Commuter Spaces | UNH Off-Campus Engagement
cards.access_notes: Specified for commuters and available during regular MUB hours.

cards.title: Commuter Kitchenette
cards.subtitle: Memorial Union Building, first floor
cards.notes: Commuting students can stop in to use the fridge or microwave and make space for lunch during regular MUB hours.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor MUB kitchenette for commuting students.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH says the first-floor MUB Commuter Kitchenette offers commuters a fridge, microwave, and a place to eat lunch.
cards.source_title: Commuter Spaces | UNH Off-Campus Engagement
cards.access_notes: Specified for commuters and available during regular MUB hours.

cards.title: Interfaith Prayer & Meditation Room
cards.subtitle: Memorial Union Building
cards.notes: Use this inclusive room for quiet prayer, contemplation, meditation, reflection, or personal practice; preserve its calm purpose.
cards.short_summary: A named MUB space for quiet reflection and practice.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH describes the MUB Interfaith Prayer & Meditation Room as an inclusive space for quiet prayer, contemplation, meditation, reflection, and practice.
cards.source_title: Venues & Services | Memorial Union & Student Activities
cards.access_notes: Use respectfully and confirm current MUB building access before visiting.

cards.title: Union Court
cards.subtitle: Memorial Union Building
cards.notes: Choose a table here to meet between classes or pair a meal stop with a conversation; check current dining operations separately.
cards.short_summary: A named MUB gathering and dining area.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH’s MUB venues page identifies Union Court as a place to eat or hang out with friends.
cards.source_title: Venues & Services | Memorial Union & Student Activities
cards.access_notes: Food purchases may be required for dining; seating and operations can vary.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten documented no-cost ways to explore art, research, science, music, and campus life at UNH Durham.

cards.title: Browse the UNH Gallery of Art
cards.subtitle: Paul Creative Arts Center, 30 Academic Way
cards.notes: Stop in during gallery hours to look through the current exhibition, then use the posted artist and exhibition details to guide your conversation.
cards.short_summary: A public campus gallery with rotating exhibitions, including student work.
cards.evidence_claim: The UNH Gallery of Art states that it is free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Gallery of Art | Art and Art History
cards.access_notes: Open daily 8 a.m.–10 p.m.; closed during university holidays, exhibition installations, and curtailed operations.

cards.entity_name: Museum of Art of the University of New Hampshire
cards.title: See the Museum of Art collection
cards.subtitle: Paul Creative Arts Center, 30 Academic Way
cards.notes: Check the museum’s current exhibition information before heading over, then spend time with a few works rather than trying to see everything at once.
cards.short_summary: A campus art museum whose public programs and galleries are documented as free.
cards.evidence_claim: The Museum of Art says that the museum and its programs are open to the public free of charge.
cards.source_title: Museum of Art of the University of New Hampshire press release
cards.access_notes: Confirm current exhibition hours before visiting.

cards.title: Look through the UNH Observatory telescope
cards.subtitle: UNH Observatory, 16 Spinney Lane
cards.notes: Arrive for a first- or third-Saturday public observing session and check the Observatory’s same-day weather update before making the walk over.
cards.short_summary: Recurring, weather-dependent public telescope sessions for all experience levels.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH lists free public observing sessions on the first and third Saturday of every month, with no appointment required.
cards.source_title: The UNH Observatory | Physics & Astronomy
cards.access_notes: Sessions can be cancelled for cloudy, rainy, or snowy conditions; check the Observatory Facebook update on the afternoon of the session.

cards.title: Go to the Fall Astronomy Festival
cards.subtitle: UNH Observatory, 16 Spinney Lane — October 16–17, 2026
cards.notes: Use the festival schedule to choose a science talk, telescope clinic, or observing block; bring a layer for nighttime activities and skip optional purchases.
cards.short_summary: A two-day UNH astronomy event with talks, demonstrations, and night-sky observing.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH states that admission to the 2026 New England Fall Astronomy Festival is free, with donations optional.
cards.source_title: New England Fall Astronomy Festival (NEFAF) | UNH Extension
cards.access_notes: October 16–17, 2026. Food, beverages, and raffle tickets are optional purchases; admission itself is free.

cards.entity_name: Ocean Discovery Day Public Open House
cards.title: Try Ocean Discovery Day activities
cards.subtitle: Jere A. Chase Ocean Engineering Laboratory, 24 Colovos Road — October 24, 2026
cards.notes: Plan a daytime visit to rotate through the hands-on stations, including ocean technology and marine-science demonstrations, without needing a ticket.
cards.short_summary: A family-friendly public open house focused on ocean science and engineering.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH describes Ocean Discovery Day’s Public Open House as a free, family-friendly event.
cards.source_title: Ocean Discovery Day Public Open House | UNH School of Marine Science and Ocean Engineering
cards.access_notes: Scheduled for Saturday, October 24, 2026, 10 a.m.–3 p.m.; parking is available at the laboratory and nearby overflow area.

cards.title: Browse the UNH Maker’s Expo
cards.subtitle: Granite State Room, Memorial Union Building — December 4, 2026
cards.notes: Walk the vendor displays to see work made by UNH students, staff, and faculty; browsing needs no ticket, and buying anything is optional.
cards.short_summary: A public maker fair featuring creative work by the UNH community.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH says the 2026 Maker’s Expo is free to enter and open to the public, with no ticket required for browsing.
cards.source_title: UNH Maker's Expo | Memorial Union & Student Activities
cards.access_notes: December 4, 2026, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; rain date December 11. Purchases from vendors are optional.

cards.title: Attend Undergraduate Research Conference events
cards.subtitle: Multiple UNH Durham venues each spring
cards.notes: Use the annual program to pick a presentation, poster session, or creative showcase that fits your interests, then arrive a few minutes early to settle in.
cards.short_summary: An annual campus-wide showcase of undergraduate research, scholarship, and creative work.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH states that all Undergraduate Research Conference events are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Undergraduate Research Conference | Hamel Center for Undergraduate Research
cards.access_notes: Review the current annual program for event times, venues, and any exceptions noted by organizers.

cards.entity_name: Saul O. Sidore Memorial Lecture Series
cards.title: Attend a Sidore Lecture
cards.subtitle: UNH Durham campus venues
cards.notes: Watch the series schedule for the next public lecture, then bring a question or talking point to carry into a post-event conversation.
cards.short_summary: A UNH humanities lecture series open to the campus and wider public.
cards.evidence_claim: The UNH Center for the Humanities states that Sidore Lecture Series lectures are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Sidore Lecture Series | UNH Center for the Humanities
cards.access_notes: Consult the series page for the next lecture’s venue, time, and any registration details.

cards.entity_name: Arlene Kies Piano Recital and Master Class Series
cards.title: Hear a Kies Series piano recital
cards.subtitle: Paul Creative Arts Center recital venues
cards.notes: Check the Music calendar for the next guest pianist or master class, then arrive early enough to find the recital space without rushing.
cards.short_summary: A recurring UNH piano performance and master-class series.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH Music states that all Arlene Kies Piano Recital and Master Class Series events are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Arlene Kies Piano Recital and Master Class Series | UNH Music
cards.access_notes: Check the current Music calendar for performance dates and specific Paul Creative Arts Center room assignments.

cards.title: Take the Campus Connector loop
cards.subtitle: UNH Durham campus shuttle stops
cards.notes: Use the current route map to link two campus stops or take a low-key loop with a friend; request pickup where the map marks on-request service.
cards.short_summary: UNH’s on-campus shuttle system serving the Durham community.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH identifies the Campus Connector as a free on-campus shuttle system open to all in the UNH Durham community.
cards.source_title: Transportation | UNH Sustainability
cards.access_notes: Use the current Campus Connector map and service notices for routes, stop locations, and operating changes.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented UNH study environments spanning quiet reading rooms, reservable project space, and specialized academic work areas.

cards.title: Addison Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Dimond Library, Level 3 main floor
cards.notes: Bring solo reading or writing here and keep calls and audible devices elsewhere; UNH designates this Level 3 room for quiet individual study.
cards.short_summary: A designated quiet-study reading room on Dimond’s main floor.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH lists the Addison Reading Room on Dimond Library Level 3 as a quiet space for individual study, where talking and audible electronic devices are not permitted.
cards.source_title: Spaces to Study & Work | Library
cards.access_notes: Located in Dimond Library; follow the library’s quiet-area expectations.

cards.title: Hubbard Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Dimond Library, Level 3 main floor
cards.notes: Use this Level 3 reading room for focused individual work, and silence devices before settling in to respect the library’s designated quiet area.
cards.short_summary: A main-floor Dimond reading room with quiet-study rules.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH identifies the Hubbard Reading Room on Dimond Library Level 3 as a designated quiet space for individual study.
cards.source_title: Spaces to Study & Work | Library
cards.access_notes: Located in Dimond Library; no talking or audible electronic devices in quiet areas.

cards.title: Courtyard Reading Room 510
cards.subtitle: Dimond Library, Level 5
cards.notes: Head to Level 5 with a single-person task and keep the room quiet; the library specifically designates the Courtyard Reading Room for individual study.
cards.short_summary: A Level 5 Dimond reading room designated for quiet work.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH lists the Courtyard Reading Room on Dimond Library Level 5 among its quiet spaces for individual study.
cards.source_title: Spaces to Study & Work | Library
cards.access_notes: Room 510 on Dimond Level 5; quiet-area rules prohibit talking and audible devices.

cards.title: Kingsbury Library Study Carrels
cards.subtitle: Kingsbury Library, right side
cards.notes: Choose a carrel on the library’s right side when you need an individual quiet-study setting, and move conversations outside the designated area.
cards.short_summary: Quiet individual-study carrels in Kingsbury Library.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH designates the study carrels on the right side of Kingsbury Library as quiet space for individual study.
cards.source_title: Spaces to Study & Work | Library
cards.access_notes: Use the study carrels on the right side of Kingsbury Library and observe quiet-area rules.

cards.title: The Study Lounge
cards.subtitle: Center for Academic Resources, Smith Hall Room 201
cards.notes: Work alongside others in this collaborative lounge, then scan the posted QR code to check in; plan around its weekday 8:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m. hours.
cards.short_summary: A collaborative CFAR study lounge open to UNH students.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH says the Study Lounge in Smith Hall Room 201 is a collaborative study space open to all UNH students and is available Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces | The Center for Academic Resources
cards.access_notes: Open to all UNH students; check in using the QR code posted on the wall. Listed hours: Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m.

cards.title: The Reset Space
cards.subtitle: Center for Academic Resources, Smith Hall Room 209
cards.notes: Use this low-stimulation room to pause, reset, or return to a focused task; relaxation resources include coloring pages and breathing guides.
cards.short_summary: A lower-stimulation CFAR space for calm focus and reset time.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH describes the Reset Space in Smith Hall Room 209 as a low-stimulation environment with relaxation resources, open to all UNH students Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces | The Center for Academic Resources
cards.access_notes: Open to all UNH students; scan the posted QR code to check in. Listed hours: Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m.

cards.title: Graduate Study Carrels
cards.subtitle: Dimond Library, Level 4, Room 441
cards.notes: Graduate students can request the room combination at the Level 3 Information Desk with a valid graduate UNH ID, then use available carrels for quiet work.
cards.short_summary: A quiet Level 4 carrel room reserved for graduate students.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH provides unassigned carrels and seating for graduate students in Dimond Library Room 441 for quiet study; a valid graduate UNH ID is required to obtain the room combination.
cards.source_title: Graduate Study Carrels | Library
cards.access_notes: For graduate students; bring a valid graduate UNH ID to the Dimond Level 3 Information Desk for the room combination.

cards.title: Studio 235
cards.subtitle: Dimond Library, Level 2
cards.notes: Reserve this room for a film-related project or presentation rehearsal; it has seating for up to 24, an 80-inch TV, playback gear, and dry-erase boards.
cards.short_summary: A reservable Level 2 media room for screening and presentation work.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH says instructors and students may reserve Studio 235 in Dimond Library; it includes tables and chairs for up to 24 people, an 80-inch TV, playback equipment, and two dry-erase boards.
cards.source_title: Studio 235 | Library
cards.access_notes: Located on Dimond Library Level 2; reserve online for film showings or related work.

cards.title: Geospatial Services Center
cards.subtitle: Dimond Library, Room 337
cards.notes: Use the seven high-performance workstations for a GIS task, and bring your UNH AD login; group consultations are welcome when they do not disrupt others.
cards.short_summary: A specialized GIS lab with high-performance workstations and support.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH’s Geospatial Services Center lab in Dimond Room 337 is open for GIS use during Dimond Library hours, has seven high-performance workstations, and primarily serves UNH students, faculty, and staff.
cards.source_title: Geospatial Services Center | Library
cards.access_notes: UNH AD login is required for the workstations; access to some software is limited to the UNH community.

cards.title: Daggett Instruction Room 421
cards.subtitle: Dimond Library, Level 4
cards.notes: Check whether the room is unbooked before using it for group work; UNH allows students to use Room 421 when it is not reserved for instruction.
cards.short_summary: A Level 4 instruction room usable by students when unbooked.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH states that Dimond Room 421 is available for faculty or staff instruction and that students may use it when it is not booked.
cards.source_title: Conference Rooms | Library
cards.access_notes: Available to students only when not booked; instruction reservations have priority, and scheduled users may need the room.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each

cards.title: Durham Public Library
cards.subtitle: Madbury Road corridor
cards.notes: Head to 49 Madbury Road to browse, use library services, or check the calendar before planning a focused off-campus stop.
cards.short_summary: A public-library stop with browsing and community services.
cards.evidence_claim: Durham Public Library is at 49 Madbury Road and lists browsing, printing, faxing, notary, and email services.
cards.source_title: Durham Public Library — Library Services
cards.access_notes: The library lists current service information online; check its hours before visiting.

cards.title: Durham House of Pizza
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the Main Street stop for a meal; the restaurant’s own page publishes its Durham address, menu link, and current stated hours.
cards.short_summary: A documented downtown pizza restaurant on Main Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Durham House of Pizza lists its location as 38 Main Street, Durham, and offers online ordering and a menu.
cards.source_title: Durham House of Pizza
cards.access_notes: Restaurant service requires a purchase; review the business’s posted hours before going.

cards.title: Breaking New Grounds
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor
cards.notes: Walk the Main Street corridor for this locally owned roastery and café, then use its posted address and hours to time a visit.
cards.short_summary: A coffee roastery and café documented at 50 Main Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Breaking New Grounds identifies itself as a locally owned coffee roastery and café at 50 Main Street in Durham.
cards.source_title: Breaking New Grounds
cards.access_notes: Food and drinks require purchase; the business posts hours on its website.

cards.title: The Freedom Café
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor

cards.short_summary: A café destination listed on Main Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town of Durham business directory lists The Freedom Café at 37 Main Street, Durham.
cards.source_title: Town of Durham Business Directory — Restaurants
cards.access_notes: Café purchases may be required; contact the business for current service details.

cards.title: UNH Dairy Bar
cards.subtitle: Depot Road corridor
cards.notes: Follow Depot Road to the named Dairy Bar, then check UNH Dining’s location information before making it your food-stop plan.
cards.short_summary: A UNH Dining destination listed at the depot.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town of Durham business directory lists The Dairy Bar at 3 Depot Road and links to its UNH Dining website.
cards.source_title: Town of Durham Business Directory — Restaurants
cards.access_notes: Food service requires purchase; verify current availability with UNH Dining.

cards.title: Durham–UNH Station
cards.subtitle: Depot Road corridor
cards.notes: Use the Depot Road rail stop as a practical landmark and consult Amtrak before travel, since schedules and ticket conditions can change.
cards.short_summary: A named rail-station destination beside downtown.
cards.evidence_claim: The Strafford Regional Planning Commission’s Durham downtown map identifies the Durham Train Station as an Amtrak Downeaster destination.
cards.source_title: Durham Downtown Business Directory Map
cards.access_notes: Rail travel requires a ticket; verify current Amtrak service and boarding details before travel.

cards.title: Hannaford - Durham
cards.subtitle: Mill Road corridor
cards.notes: Use Mill Road for a grocery stop; Hannaford’s store page provides the Durham address, phone number, and currently posted daily hours.
cards.short_summary: A full grocery-store destination at 7 Mill Road.
cards.evidence_claim: Hannaford lists its Durham store at 7 Mill Road with daily hours of 7:00 AM–9:00 PM.
cards.source_title: Hannaford — Durham, New Hampshire
cards.access_notes: Shopping requires purchase; the store page lists daily hours but confirm before visiting.

cards.title: The Works Bakery Café
cards.subtitle: Mill Road corridor
cards.notes: Make this a Mill Road food stop when its café service fits your plans; the town directory places it at 5A Mill Road Plaza.
cards.short_summary: A named bakery-café destination in Mill Road Plaza.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town of Durham business directory lists Works Bakery Cafe at 5A Mill Road Plaza, Durham.
cards.source_title: Town of Durham Business Directory — Restaurants
cards.access_notes: Café food and beverages require purchase; confirm current service with the business.

cards.title: Bamee
cards.subtitle: Jenkins Court corridor
cards.notes: Take the short Jenkins Court detour for this named restaurant destination, using the town’s address listing to orient your walk.
cards.short_summary: A restaurant destination on Jenkins Court.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town of Durham business directory lists Bamee at 12 Jenkins Court, Suite 1, Durham.
cards.source_title: Town of Durham Business Directory — Restaurants
cards.access_notes: Restaurant dining requires purchase; confirm current service directly with the restaurant.

cards.title: Three Chimneys Inn
cards.subtitle: Newmarket Road corridor
cards.notes: Use Newmarket Road for a historic-inn landmark and dining destination; the town directory identifies the property and its street address.
cards.short_summary: An inn and restaurant destination on Newmarket Road.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town of Durham business directory lists Three Chimneys Inn as lodging and restaurant at 17 Newmarket Road, Durham.
cards.source_title: Town of Durham Business Directory — Restaurants
cards.access_notes: Dining and lodging require purchase; check the inn directly for current availability.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented UNH traditions, mixing current Wildcat rituals with clearly labeled historical practices preserved by UNH Libraries.

cards.title: Pat the Cat
cards.subtitle: Wildcat statue, UNH Durham campus
cards.notes: Stop by the Wildcat statue and rub its nose for good luck; UNH admissions describes the ritual as spanning campus tours through graduation.
cards.short_summary: A current good-luck ritual centered on UNH’s Wildcat statue.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH Admissions documents “pat the cat” as rubbing the Wildcat statue’s nose for good luck throughout a student’s UNH journey.
cards.source_title: Favorite Tour Stop | Undergraduate Admissions
cards.access_notes: The source identifies the Wildcat statue as the setting; check campus access conditions before visiting.

cards.title: Fish on the Ice
cards.subtitle: UNH hockey at the Whittemore Center
cards.notes: Watch for the first UNH hockey goal: the university’s visitor guide identifies fish on the ice as the signal that the Wildcats have scored.
cards.short_summary: A hockey-goal tradition with an unmistakably fishy visual cue.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH’s Whittemore Center tour states that fish on the ice means UNH hockey scored its first goal.
cards.source_title: Whittemore Center | Explore the University of New Hampshire
cards.access_notes: Observe venue and event rules; this card documents the tradition and does not instruct visitors to throw objects.

cards.title: The Freshman Beanie Era
cards.subtitle: Historical UNH tradition — ended with the Class of 1971
cards.notes: See the archive record of blue freshman caps with white buttons, once used to identify newcomers and build class spirit.
cards.short_summary: A long-running freshman identifier, now a documented archive tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH’s museum says freshman beanies began in 1909 and that the Class of 1971 was the last required to wear one.
cards.source_title: Out of the Cat's Closet: The University Museum's Unique Collection
cards.access_notes: Historical and discontinued; view the university archive material rather than attempting to revive a requirement.

cards.title: Carry a Senior Cane
cards.subtitle: Historical UNH graduation custom — replaced in 1940
cards.notes: Explore the archival images of seniors carrying canes in their final weeks, often marked by classmates as personal mementos.
cards.short_summary: Graduation-era walking canes preceded UNH’s senior-ring custom.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH Libraries records that senior canes symbolized impending graduation and were replaced with a senior ring in 1940.
cards.source_title: Out of the Cat's Closet: The University Museum's Unique Collection
cards.access_notes: Historical and discontinued; the source includes an archival photograph of seniors with a class cane.

cards.title: The Main Street Rules Posters
cards.subtitle: Historical UNH custom along Main Street
cards.notes: Read the archive’s account of sophomores posting first-year rules overnight along Main Street before the start of classes.
cards.short_summary: A former class-rivalry ritual documented by UNH’s museum.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH Libraries documents that sophomores wrote and posted Freshman Rules posters along Main Street for freshmen to remove or obey.
cards.source_title: Out of the Cat's Closet: The University Museum's Unique Collection
cards.access_notes: Historical only; do not post materials on campus property or recreate class-enforcement practices.

cards.title: Build the Field on New Hampshire Day
cards.subtitle: Historical campus workday — 1916 to 1924
cards.notes: Trace the 1916 campus-wide workday when classes paused and students and faculty improved what is now Memorial Field.
cards.short_summary: A former all-campus labor day devoted to the athletic field.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH Libraries states that the first New Hampshire Day was held in 1916 and the annual event continued until 1924.
cards.source_title: The Way We Were: A Collection of UNH Anecdotes
cards.access_notes: Historical and discontinued; use the archive exhibit to learn about the event.

cards.title: Elect a “Mayor” of Durham
cards.subtitle: Historical Homecoming tradition — 1926 through the 1960s
cards.notes: Follow the archive account of student mayoral campaigns, voting under Thompson Hall’s arch, and a Homecoming-game ceremonial winner.
cards.short_summary: A former student election that turned Homecoming into mock civic theater.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH Libraries says Mayor of Durham campaigns began in 1926, continued into the 1960s, and the winner appeared at the Homecoming football game.
cards.source_title: Bulls, Wildcats & Mayors: Sports & Social Traditions
cards.access_notes: Historical and discontinued; Thompson Hall is referenced as the former voting location.

cards.title: Winter Carnival’s Ski-Jump Origins
cards.subtitle: Historical UNH winter-sports tradition — begun in 1922
cards.notes: Use the museum exhibit to follow the Forestry Club’s first carnival, then the Outing Club’s expanded winter games and carnival ball.
cards.short_summary: UNH’s early winter festival combined outdoor competition and social events.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH Libraries documents the first Winter Carnival in 1922 and its later Outing Club sponsorship with winter sports and snow-related games.
cards.source_title: Bulls, Wildcats & Mayors: Sports & Social Traditions
cards.access_notes: Historical exhibit material; the source describes the original locations and activities.

cards.title: Casque and Casket’s Spring Dance
cards.subtitle: Historical inter-fraternity event — formed in 1905
cards.notes: Read the archival description of this senior-junior society’s annual spring dance and its theatrical opening procession with a casket.
cards.short_summary: A notably theatrical former spring social event preserved in UNH archives.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH Libraries identifies Casque and Casket as an inter-fraternity senior-junior society formed in 1905 and describes its annual spring dance.
cards.source_title: The Way We Were: A Collection of UNH Anecdotes
cards.access_notes: Historical only; the source is an archive exhibit describing the former event.

cards.entity_name: Wildcat Marching Band AlumniBand at Homecoming
cards.title: Bring AlumniBand Back for Homecoming
cards.subtitle: Wildcat Marching Band tradition at UNH Homecoming
cards.notes: Look for the Wildcat Marching Band’s AlumniBand at Homecoming, one of the traditions listed in the band’s official handbook.
cards.short_summary: A band-community Homecoming tradition that reconnects alumni performers.
cards.evidence_claim: The UNH Wildcat Marching Band handbook lists hosting AlumniBand at Homecoming among the organization’s continuing traditions.
cards.source_title: Wildcat Marching Band Handbook
cards.access_notes: Confirm current Homecoming and band-event details with UNH before attending.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of New Hampshire, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure first-weekend loop through central campus, its study and arts spaces, recreation, food, and nearby woods.

cards.title: Start at the MUB
cards.subtitle: Campus-life hub, Durham campus
cards.notes: Use the Memorial Union Building as your first indoor landmark: check the public activity listings, orient yourself, and choose a next stop together.
cards.short_summary: A central starting point for campus activities and services.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH identifies the Memorial Union Building as a place where Wildcats gather for events, activities, and everyday hangout.
cards.source_title: Durham Campus | University of New Hampshire
cards.access_notes: Building and departmental schedules vary; confirm access on the MUB site before visiting.

cards.title: Play a quick round in the Games Room
cards.subtitle: Room 154A, Memorial Union Building
cards.notes: Bring a new acquaintance to MUB room 154A for billiards, table tennis, or video games; ask staff about availability when you arrive.
cards.short_summary: A named MUB room for casual games.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH says the Games Room in MUB room 154A offers billiards, table tennis, and video games.
cards.source_title: Venues & Services | Memorial Union & Student Activities
cards.access_notes: Equipment and room availability may vary; check with the MUB during its open hours.

cards.title: Meet at the Wildcat Sculpture
cards.subtitle: Street side of Memorial Field
cards.notes: Make the bronze Wildcat Sculpture a simple outdoor photo-and-meetup point before continuing across campus; keep clear of any athletic activity nearby.
cards.short_summary: A documented bronze wildcat artwork beside Memorial Field.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH Library documents that the bronze Wildcat Sculpture is on the street side of Memorial Field and was unveiled during 2006 Homecoming Weekend.
cards.source_title: UNH Mascots | Library
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public artwork; observe it from pedestrian areas and follow posted event controls.

cards.title: Find your bearings at Dimond Library
cards.subtitle: 18 Library Way, Durham
cards.notes: Walk through the main Durham library, locate the information desk, and note a quiet floor or service you may want to use during the semester.
cards.short_summary: UNH’s main Durham library, with research collections and student-facing services.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH identifies Ezekiel W. Dimond Library as the main library on the Durham campus and lists its collections, Special Collections, and University Archives.
cards.source_title: Dimond Library | UNH Library
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current hours before arrival; services and floor access can vary.

cards.title: See what is hanging at the UNH Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: Paul Creative Arts Center
cards.notes: Drop into the UNH Art Gallery during regular business hours and look for the current exhibition; pair the visit with a walk around the arts center.
cards.short_summary: A free gallery in the Paul Creative Arts Center.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH states that the UNH Art Gallery is in the Paul Creative Arts Center and has free admission during regular business hours.
cards.source_title: Latest on the UNH Art Gallery
cards.access_notes: Free during regular business hours; exhibitions and access may change, so confirm before going.

cards.title: Take a daylight walk in College Woods
cards.subtitle: West side of the main campus
cards.notes: Use the documented main entrance for a daytime walk, jog, or bird-watch; stay on suitable routes and bring layers for changing New Hampshire weather.
cards.short_summary: A 250-acre university woodland used for recreation and teaching.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH describes College Woods as about 250 acres on the west side of main campus, with hiking, walking, skiing, jogging, bird watching, and relaxation among its recreational uses.
cards.source_title: College Woods | UNH College of Life Sciences and Agriculture
cards.access_notes: Use the official directions and visit in daylight; hiking and biking have different allowed areas.

cards.title: Scope out Hamel Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: 5 Edgewood Road, Durham
cards.notes: Visit the Hamel Recreation Center welcome area to learn how campus recreation access works and choose a future class, facility, or outdoor activity.
cards.short_summary: The campus recreation entry point for student membership and facility access.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH’s Campus Recreation student membership page lists Hamel Recreation Center among fall and spring membership benefits for eligible students.
cards.source_title: Campus Recreation Student Membership | UNH Campus Recreation
cards.access_notes: Ask the welcome center about eligibility and current facility schedules; access depends on membership or enrollment status.

cards.title: Plan a warm-weather pool visit
cards.subtitle: Accessed through Hamel Recreation Center
cards.notes: If it is in season, review the pool schedule first, then bring swim gear for a relaxed lap or free-swim session with friends.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal UNH pool with lap lanes and free-swim space.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH describes the Outdoor Pool as having zero-depth entry, swim lanes, and space for free swimming, with entrance through Hamel Recreation Center.
cards.source_title: Outdoor Pool | UNH Campus Recreation
cards.access_notes: Season is late June through early September, weather permitting; check the current facility calendar and access eligibility.

cards.title: Have a meal at Holloway Commons
cards.subtitle: Central campus dining hall
cards.notes: Use a meal swipe or pay at the counter for a first shared campus meal; review the live menu and allergen information before choosing a station.
cards.short_summary: UNH’s centrally located largest dining hall.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH identifies Holloway Commons as its largest, centrally located dining hall and states that students can enter dining halls with fingerprint ID or by paying at the counter.
cards.source_title: Admitted Students Guide: Campus Dining | Undergraduate Admissions
cards.access_notes: Meal swipe or payment is required; current menus and schedules may change for holidays and events.

cards.title: Check the Dairy Bar’s seasonal opening
cards.subtitle: 3 Depot Road, Durham
cards.notes: When it is open, stop at the Dairy Bar for food or ice cream and take note of its historic train-station setting near the Durham depot.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal UNH dining location in a historic train-station building.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH Dining lists the Dairy Bar at 3 Depot Road and notes that its hours can change; UNH Archives documents that it is housed in the historic train station.
cards.source_title: UNH Dairy Bar | Dining
cards.access_notes: Currently seasonal; verify current opening dates and hours on UNH Dining before making the walk.
